analyst_view.overall: Levante (16th, 12 pts, one point above the drop and four league games without a win) host Racing Santander (8th, 17 pts, back-to-back wins over Málaga and Real Sociedad) on Friday night; the numbers make it a clear home win with about 3.8 goals. Luís Castro's side drew 1-1 with Elche on Monday, so they get four days' rest, and they have lost both full-backs: Manu Sánchez has a torn cruciate ligament (out for the season, not in the numbers) and Jeremy Toljan a hamstring injury (2-3 weeks, now in the numbers), so 16-year-old Marc Santos and Nacho Pérez are expected to start. José Alberto's Racing have only 3 points away from home and have conceded 19 goals on their travels; Mantilla, Gueye and Andrés Martín are out and already counted, and the starters were eased through training on Tuesday. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, 2.5 for Levante. Yesterday I leaned a little lower because Levante's attack is blunt, but their ratings already see that, and the new detail points the other way: Racing have conceded 19 goals away from home, and Levante now play a 16-year-old at left-back with Manu Sánchez out for the season, which should help Racing score too. The two pull against each other, so I move back to the numbers' 3.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, 7.0 for Levante. Racing concede plenty of corners (40 in their last six), which the numbers already count, and Levante attack down the wings with Brugué and Thiago Fernández; with a teenage left-back Levante may push less down that side, but that is a guess. Nothing clear either way, so I stay at about 11.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already a little lower for both sides' recent bookings. Levante are fighting to stay up and two of their centre-backs, Mandi and De la Fuente, are one booking from a ban, which may make them more careful; Racing are comfortable in mid-table and no referee is named yet. Nothing the numbers can't see points clearly, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.6 shots, already lifted for Racing's busy recent games (+11.2% on their side). Levante's short rest and stand-in full-backs could take a little off their shooting, but Racing let opponents shoot freely away from home, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at about 34.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already lowered for Levante's poor recent accuracy (-4.5%) and raised for Racing's (+4.3%, with Zabiri on 11 goals). Racing's leaky away defence and Levante's patched full-backs point to chances at both ends, which the numbers already expect, so I stay at 10.5.
